title: The 10 Best Mechanic Stools
subtitle: Pneumatic and low rolling mechanic stools and creeper seats, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A rolling mechanic stool saves your knees and back on brake jobs, detailing and anything at wheel height. We ranked 10 best-sellers from Pro-LifT, MaxWorks, WEN, BIG RED, VEVOR and others on rating, review volume and features (pneumatic height, a tool tray, a 300 lb rating and five casters).

changelog.note: Prices, ratings and review counts re-checked on every listing. Biggest price moves: the BIG RED TR63002 rose from $30.74 to $36.57.
Page published with 10 ranked picks and 1 tool to avoid.

products.name: Pro-LifT PL9300H Pneumatic Rolling Mechanic Chair
products.verdict: The most-reviewed stool here: a pneumatic seat that adjusts 5 inches, five casters, a segmented tool tray and a 300 lb rating, rated 4.6 stars on 7,460 reviews.

avoid.name: JOSTZHXIN Low Height Roller Stool, Height Adjustable, for Salon, Spa, Home, Office and Garage (H05)
avoid.flag: Salon stool claiming 400 lb; no tray
avoid.verdict: A small salon-style stool sold as a mechanic stool, with a weight rating higher than any purpose-built garage stool here.
reasons: Its spec table lists a 400 lb maximum on a small round seat, more than the 300 lb steel-framed mechanic stools from Pro-LifT, MaxWorks and WEN.
It's pitched for 'salon, spa, home office' as much as the garage, and has no tool tray.
It says it 'can be a low rolling stool, also can be a high stool', but adjusts only from 16.1 to 18.7 inches. The MaxWorks 80771 costs less with a tray and a 15 to 20 inch range.

buyers_guide.a: A pneumatic stool adjusts with a lever, usually 15 to 20 inches, which suits brake jobs and bumper work. Fixed creeper seats sit lower and cost less.
Five casters are more stable than four, especially when you lean. Bigger casters roll over cords and cracks more easily.

buyers_guide.q: Do I need a tool tray?
buyers_guide.a: A tray under the seat keeps sockets and fasteners with you as you roll around the car. It's one of the most useful features.
Choose a stool rated comfortably above your weight. Most mechanic stools are rated 250 or 300 lb.
Low stools for wheel work rarely have backs. For long sessions at a workbench, a taller stool with a backrest is more comfortable.
